user_goal: Buy a product that is sold only in whole packs and always see the price of a pack, never a confusing per-piece figure.
business_goal: Sell sticker-like consumables in packs so shopping-channel listings advertise a real purchasable price, with the feed, the landing page and the charged amount all equal.

user_journey.step: Browse a category and see pack pricing on the card
Open the product and pick a pack tier
Add whole packs to the cart and adjust in pack steps
Review the order and confirm totals match the server
See the confirmed order expressed in packs
Arrive from a shopping channel on a preselected configuration

happy_path.action: Open the Stickers & Labels category listing and read the Custom Die-Cut Stickers card price block
happy_path.expected_result: Card shows the pack 'From' price (price_from x pack_size = Rs 300.00) with the caption 'per 50 pcs' instead of a per-unit caption; discount percent rendering unchanged.

happy_path.action: Open the product detail page and read the pricing tier rows
happy_path.selector: PricingTable rows: text '50 pcs · ₹750' with secondary '₹15.00/pc'
happy_path.expected_result: Each row label is '<quantity> pcs · <pack total>' with a '₹X/pc' secondary line; multi-pack rows also show '· N packs'. Pack total equals rounded unit price x quantity exactly.

happy_path.action: Select the 5-pack (250 pcs) tier and read the configurator summary
happy_path.selector: PricingTable row for quantity 250; ProductConfigurator summary
happy_path.expected_result: Summary expresses the selection as '5 packs (250 pcs)' and the total equals the backend's compute_item_pricing total for quantity 250.

happy_path.action: Add the selected configuration to the cart and open the cart drawer
happy_path.selector: Add to Cart button; CartDrawerItem quantity label
happy_path.expected_result: Drawer line reads '5 packs (250 pcs)' via formatQuantity, not a bare '250'.

happy_path.action: Press the drawer quantity increase and decrease controls once each
happy_path.expected_result: Quantity moves by one whole pack (250 -> 300 -> 250), never by the legacy 25/50 steps, and never below one pack (50).

happy_path.action: Open the full cart page and read the line quantity and stepper
happy_path.selector: app/cart/page.tsx line quantity span; stepper buttons
happy_path.expected_result: Line shows formatQuantity pack text and the stepper steps in whole packs with a one-pack floor.

happy_path.action: Go to checkout and compare the review-step totals against the backend order preview
happy_path.selector: features/checkout/ReviewStep.tsx line quantity + order summary totals
happy_path.expected_result: Line reads '5 packs (250 pcs)' via formatQuantityLine; displayed totals equal the server preview exactly, so no price_changed banner appears and no price-mismatch telemetry event is created.

happy_path.action: Place the order with the dev/fake payment provider and read the confirmation page
happy_path.expected_result: Confirmed order line is expressed in packs from the snapshotted pack_size/unit_label on the order item.

alternate_paths.path_name: Arrive from the shopping feed on a preselected configuration

steps.action: Open the PDP with the exact query string from the product's listing_offer (qty=50&size=2-x-2-in-square&paper=vinyl-matte&finish=diecut&sides=single-sided&turnaround=standard)
steps.expected_result: The 1-pack (50 pcs) tier and each named size/paper/finish/sides/turnaround option are selected on arrival, and the displayed total equals listing_offer.price (Rs 750.00), i.e. the feed's g:price.

steps.action: Read the JSON-LD block emitted on that same PDP
steps.expected_result: offers is a single Offer (not AggregateOffer) whose price equals the same listing_offer value, with priceCurrency INR, availability, itemCondition and seller; product name carries the 'Pack of 50 pcs' suffix.

steps.action: Open a pack_size=1 product's card, PDP and cart line
steps.expected_result: Card caption, PDP tier rows, cart quantity text and the legacy 25/50 cart steppers all render exactly as before pack selling existed; no pack or unit-label text anywhere.

error_paths.trigger: PDP opened with unknown or malformed preselect params (qty=37, size=not-a-size, turnaround=bogus)
error_paths.expected_ui_response: Every unresolvable value is dropped and the configurator keeps its defaults; the page renders normally with no error and no console exception.

error_paths.trigger: Server returns 422 invalid_pack_multiple for a cart or order request whose quantity is not a whole number of packs
error_paths.expected_ui_response: The coded message from lib/api/validationErrors.ts is surfaced and the shopper is sent back to the cart rather than left on a dead checkout step.

error_paths.trigger: A persisted guest cart holds a legacy non-multiple quantity (e.g. 120 pcs of a pack-50 product) and is synced on load
error_paths.expected_ui_response: The server snaps the line to the nearest whole pack and returns quantityCorrected with originalQuantity; the store adopts the corrected quantity and shows exactly one toast 'Quantity adjusted to full packs (was 120)'.
error_paths.selector: features/cart/CartSyncProvider.tsx toast copy; features/cart/store.ts fix merge

edge_cases.case: MRP is set per pack, so the strikethrough must be the pack MRP and not the per-unit MRP
edge_cases.existing_validation: getFromPackPrice in lib/utils.ts and PriceDisplay render mrpFromPack / packPrice(mrp, packSize); percent off is computed from the same pair
edge_cases.risk_note: A float multiplication here would drift by a paisa at large pack sizes; lib/pack.ts packPrice multiplies in integer cents specifically to avoid that. Worth asserting the struck figure equals mrp_per_unit x pack_size exactly.

edge_cases.case: Pack price must equal the amount actually charged, including option multipliers
edge_cases.existing_validation: PricingTable uses the configurator's priceTier total (already unit-rounded) rather than recomputing pack x multiplier
edge_cases.risk_note: Spec section 11 allows option multipliers to move the pack figure by up to pack_size x 0.005 versus 'base pack x multiplier'. Display must follow the charge, not the other way round.

edge_cases.case: Cart store rehydration before useMounted renders SSR defaults
edge_cases.existing_validation: useMounted gate in HeaderActions / MobileBottomNav per the repo's hydration rule
edge_cases.risk_note: A screenshot or assertion taken too early reads 0 items and would make pack quantity text look missing when it is merely not hydrated yet.

edge_cases.case: Stepping down repeatedly must floor at one pack, never 0 or a partial pack
edge_cases.existing_validation: stepQuantity -> Math.max(size, base - size) in lib/pack.ts
edge_cases.risk_note: A 0 or partial quantity would be rejected by the backend with invalid_pack_multiple on the next write, turning a UI slip into a failed checkout.

edge_cases.case: Pack data absent from a stale backend response or an old persisted cart entry
edge_cases.existing_validation: normalizePack defaults to size 1 / 'pcs' for anything non-integer or < 1
edge_cases.risk_note: Without the default, a pack-aware stepper would divide by undefined and strand the line at NaN.

gaps: GET /api/v1/feeds/products.xml cannot be exercised over HTTP locally: resolve_link_base rejects a localhost FRONTEND_URL, so the route returns 503 feed_not_configured. Feed body content is therefore verified through the backend suite (tests/api/test_shopping_feed.py) and an in-process render against the dev DB, not through the storefront.
The storefront never reads quantity_steps (deprecated per spec D6), so there is nothing to assert for it on this side.

Price sorting and min/max price filters remain per-unit by design (spec D5), so a mixed-pack-size card list can legitimately look unsorted by pack price; this is a documented limitation, not a testable defect.
